description: The observer in `text(tail($)) = "b"` reads the original input through the span projection. The chosen a elides T at 0 and at 2, so the reconstructed input is T A B T, and c reads both synthetic T as bare terminals. a survives only if tail($) drops the original A token; then a and c are two readings. Read over the reconstructed tokens, tail($) drops the leading synthetic and keeps "a b", a is lost, and c alone would pass (engine §7.5).
grammar:
%ambiguity-resolution late-elision elision-only
%elidable T
%rule text a | b | c
%rule a [T="ta"] $x(pair) [T="ta"]
%conditions text(tail($)) = "b"
%rule b [T="ta"] [T="ta"] pair [T="ta"]
%rule c T="ta" pair T="ta"
%rule pair A B
%rule term T
